correctness.rationale: Exact four-subspace decomposition of direction-weighted Kronecker-sum Laplacian, PBH, cycle-space/leaf elimination, and rank-two centered component equations prove all-S iff criterion. Finite incidence forest bound proves minimum, and explicit selected sets realize it in both resonance regimes; matrix-tree theorem gives enumeration. Fully reconstructed for p,q>=2 and a,b>0. Standalone script exhaustively checks 4,944 masks across five boards twice and verifies 11,378 assertions, but analytical proof (not computation) covers arbitrary dimensions.

originality.rationale: The novel component assessed is the complete if-and-only-if graph characterization of every terminal vertex selection on weighted rook networks, including the precise collision-dependent component-count determinant, sharp constructions, and enumeration of nonresonant optimal placements. The general product eigenspace formula (2012/2020), PBH, incidence forest-cycle test, and maximum-multiplicity principle (2013) are acknowledged as prior; novelty is not claimed for those ingredients in isolation. Published full-text comparisons and topic/alias/duality searches did not show equivalent combined coverage. Remaining risk: unindexed discrete-design or observability literature could contain an equivalent criterion.
residual_risks: An unindexed specialized rook-graph observability source or a two-way design-of-experiments article might present an equivalent forest-and-resonance criterion under other terminology.
The zero-forcing 2014 source was checked at abstract level only and cannot support whole-document absence; this is not decisive because strong-structural quantifiers differ.
The broad Yuan et al. multiplicity principle likely covers the minimum-input-number corollary at some level; that cardinality alone is not an originality basis.

value.rationale: A natural fixed-Laplacian vertex-actuator problem on high-symmetry rectangular networks receives a linear-time combinatorial test for every selection, an exact degeneracy-sensitive component rule and a sharp minimum-placement design for every pair of side sizes. A simple spectral multiplicity number cannot distinguish the resonant failure of a rectangular patch from a same-cardinality valid switched patch; the determinant condition and spanning-tree enumeration make that design gap explicit.
